Hi Emma — great to hear you're moving forward. Quick answers up front, then I'll outline a proposed short plan:

1) Short-text priming: we recommend a hybrid approach — prefix-augmentation (add category / context tokens before the SKU), and a lightweight pseudo-feedback reranker pass using cached exemplars for the same category. This preserves short token signal while giving the model more context for relevance scoring.

2) Vector DBs: Redwood's backfill tooling supports Milvus and Pinecone, but there are trade-offs we want to review with your infra team (index config portability, shard sizing, TTLs). We'll need to validate your Milvus build and storage class.

Proposed 3-step pilot plan (30–45 days):
- Week 0: Validation — run a compatibility matrix and small hydra test (10k rows) against your Milvus cluster.
- Week 1–2: Seed + priming calibration — create a seed set (5–10% of priority SKUs) and run priming experiments, produce rerank candidate distributions.
- Week 3–4: Backfill & smoke tests — full backfill to new index (if migrating) or augment existing Milvus index with Redwood-compatible metadata and run rerank acceptance tests.

I'm looping in Marissa (implementation) and Monica (CS ops) to outline tasks and risks. Can you share a contact on infra who can grant a short window to run the hydra test?

Thanks,
Lukas
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Emma — thanks for the note. I put together an implementation checklist and attached three artifacts: a) initial_seed_policy.md (how we pick seed docs and priming exemplars), b) nimbus_rerank_sample_prompts.csv (your sample prompts annotated), and c) vector_db_compatibility_matrix.xlsx (details we typically collect).

Operational notes from the checklist:
- Access: we only need read+write service account for a 48-hour window to run the hydra compatibility check. No production writes unless you approve the cutover.
- Seed policy: start with 5% of high-traffic SKUs + 100 category exemplars. Manual review gate before full backfill.
- Rerank evals: use A/B holdout with at least 50k queries over two weeks for signal stability; primary metric = normalized reciprocal rank (NRR), secondary = click-through delta.
- Rollback: if NRR degrades >1.5% we pause and roll back to cached baseline within 30 minutes.

Risk log (top entries):
1) Short-token ambiguity — mitigated by category prefixing and exemplar priming.
2) Index compatibility — possible mismatch in Milvus index params that require a lightweight reindex.
3) Throughput — backfill could spike IO; recommend throttled ingestion and a maintenance window.

Questions for your infra team:
- Milvus version and storage class (ephemeral vs. persistent SSD)?
- Current shard/replica config and average vector dim.
- Any existing TTL/purging rules we should honor?
